operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: Hereafter no person is accorded a classified civil-service status on the basis of his name having been reached on a civil-service register unless he was regularly selected for appointment from a certificate for probational appointment and entered on duty under it, or unless (a) he was appointed to a classified (competitive) position other than temporary-job employment of one year or less, (b) before March 16, 1942 (positions generally) or October 23, 1943 (Post Office field service), and (c) the Commission's records clearly show he stood higher on an appropriate list than another eligible who received an original probational appointment from it; the order supersedes EO 9506 but does not supersede or modify EO 9538. Ended with the whole order: EO 9830 Part III revokes it by number, effective 1947-05-01 under EO 9830's enacting clause. The order has no sunset, term or termination clause of its own; 'Hereafter' fixes its start, and the March 16, 1942 and October 23, 1943 dates limit the class of persons, not the life of the order. No amendment, extension, suspension or earlier partial end of this clause by any other instrument was found before 1947-05-01 (D6), so no later event is attached.

By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by section 17fÌ3 of the Revised Statutes of 
the United States and by section 2 of the 
Civil Service Act (22 Stat. 403), it is 
hereby ordered as follows:
Hereafter no person shall be accorded 
a classified civil-service status on the ba­
sis of his name having been reached on 
a civil-service register unless he shall 
have been regularly selected for appoint­
ment from a certificate issued by the 
Civil Service Commission for probational 
appointment and shall have entered on 
duty pursuant to selection from such 
certificate, or unless (a) he shall have 
been appointed to a classified (competi­
tive) position for other than temporary- 
job employment lasting for one year or 
less, (b) his appointment shall have been 
prior to March 16, 1942, with respect to 
positions generally or prior to October 
23, 1943, with respect to positions in the 
field service of the Post Office Depart­
ment, and (c) the records of the Civil 
Service Commission clearly show that he 
stood higher on an appropriate civil- 
service list of eligibles than another eligi­
ble who received an original probational 
appointment from such list.
This order supersedes Executive Order 
No. 9506 of December 12,19441 ; but does 
not supersede or modify Executive Order 
No. 9538 of April 13, 1945.*

research_rationale: EO 9598 (signed 1945-08-17, 10 FR 10158, FR issue of 1945-08-21), read in full from the held official FR text: one operative paragraph setting the conditions on which a classified status may be accorded on the basis of a name reached on a register, plus a supersession sentence. The dossier clause 5489-6814 was checked and confirmed as the complete inventory: it begins at the enacting clause immediately after the EO 9598 heading (offset 5385) and ends at '... No. 9538 of April 13, 1945.*' before the signature; the neighbouring EO 9599 text on the same page lies outside it. It is revoked by number in EO 9830 Part III, effective 1947-05-01 (the enacting clause 'effective May 1, 1947' governs Part III; signing and FR filing on 1947-02-24 are not the effective date). The ACT record ACT:EO:9598>EO:9830 is an agent-located record upheld by an independent AI reviewer with a D6 step (simulated ingestion; not yet in the committed build). D6 / earlier-end test (did any instrument other than EO 9830 end the order or a clause before 1947-05-01?): The order has no sunset, term or termination clause of its own; 'Hereafter' fixes its start, and the March 16, 1942 and October 23, 1943 dates limit the class of persons, not the life of the order. The by-number scan of all held FR order texts finds 9598 only in EO 9598/9599/9600 (same FR issue) and EO 9830 (Part III row); the other hits are coincidental (EO 10186 a page number, EO 10687/10688 F.R. Doc. 56-9598, EO 14075 a file hash). The OFR catalog edges for EO 9598 record only its own supersession of EO 9506, the 'See' cross-references with EO 9538, and the EO 9830 revocation. The dossier gap 'target provision not located: EO:9538' is that cross-reference: EO 9538 (1945-04-13) is earlier than EO 9598 and cannot act on it; EO 9598 itself says it 'does not supersede or modify' EO 9538. EO 9691 (1946-02-04, held, read secs. 3, 5, 6, 8, 9) creates a separate route to status (sec. 6, on recommendation after a register is established) and a status route for disabled veterans (sec. 8); neither names EO 9598 nor amends its standing condition, so they overlap without ending it. Residual coverage note: the held FR corpus holds only FR issues that carry an executive order, so Civil Service Commission regulations published elsewhere are not searchable; no instrument found suggests a Commission act could end a presidential order. The order was not attacked by any other held instrument before 1947-05-01. No earlier end of the order or of any clause was found, so every clause is terminated on 1947-05-01 and no later event is attached. Savings: transferred_or_accrued (see savings_residuals). AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record for EO 9830 (held FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9830.txt, text_sha256 b519c570..., 12 FR 1259 ff., read for this purpose: enacting clause, Parts I-III and every revocation row): the enacting clause 'it is hereby ordered as follows, effective May 1, 1947:' (offsets 2164-2220) governs Parts I (Civil Service Rules), II (Schedules) and III; Part III (from offset 90277) is the single sentence 'The following Executive orders are hereby revoked:' followed by a one-per-line list of orders, with no exception, savings, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording; a search of the whole text for 'shall not affect', 'heretofore', 'pending', 'nothing herein', 'remain in effect', 'continue in effect' and 'supersed' finds no savings clause for revoked orders (the only 'heretofore' hit, at 30777, concerns persons appointed under the new Rule III sec. 3.2). Own-residual check, reading EO 9598 in full: it is a standing condition on according classified status; status already accorded before 1947-05-01 is a completed act, not a continuing effect of the order. EO 9830 replaces the subject with its own Rule III: sec. 3.1(b)(5) and (6) (offset 28094 ff.) let an employee who was serving when his name was reached on an appropriate register acquire competitive status if recommended before the register expires, or if appointed to a competitive position before it was placed under the War Service Regulations and he stood higher than another eligible who received an original probational appointment. That is re-enactment of the subject by the successor order on the same date, not continuation of EO 9598: transferred_or_accrued. EO 9830 has no savings clause reaching it. Nothing of EO 9598 itself outlives its revocation. Bounded search: the order and EO 9830 read in full in the held official FR texts; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts; every hit read in context); the OFR catalog edges for the order (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv); a check of catalog titles of unheld orders between the order and EO 9830 for any personnel-rule change; the three machine searches (OFR catalog, U.S. Code, eCFR) read with their scope notes.

The ACT record ACT:EO:9688>EO:9830 is an agent-located record upheld by an independent AI reviewer with a D6 step (simulated ingestion; not yet in the committed build). The by-number scan of all held FR order texts finds 9688 only in EO 9688/9689 (same FR issue; the Commission cross-reference 'For an amendment of § 51.8 see Executive Order 9688, supra') and EO 9830 (Part III row); the other hits are coincidental (EO 9773 a sugar-order page number, EO 11051 a page number, EO 11011 a file hash). savings_residuals.reason: Reading record for EO 9830 (held FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9830.txt, text_sha256 b519c570..., 12 FR 1259 ff., read for this purpose: enacting clause, Parts I-III and every revocation row): the enacting clause 'it is hereby ordered as follows, effective May 1, 1947:' (offsets 2164-2220) governs Parts I (Civil Service Rules), II (Schedules) and III; Part III (from offset 90277) is the single sentence 'The following Executive orders are hereby revoked:' followed by a one-per-line list of orders, with no exception, savings, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording; a search of the whole text for 'shall not affect', 'heretofore', 'pending', 'nothing herein', 'remain in effect', 'continue in effect' and 'supersed' finds no savings clause for revoked orders (the only 'heretofore' hit, at 30777, concerns persons appointed under the new Rule III sec. 3.2). Own-residual check, reading EO 9688 in full: it placed a class of positions in Schedule B; appointments made under it before 1947-05-01 are completed acts. EO 9830 Part II re-lists the same class in its own new Schedule B: '(8) Navy Department, (i) Positions assigned exclusively to Navy Communications Intelligence Activities.' (EO 9830 text offset 88007). That is re-enactment by the successor order on the same date, not continuation of EO 9688: the clause ends and its subject is carried forward, transferred_or_accrued. EO 9830 has no savings clause reaching it.
